title: Domain-decomposed Evolutional Deep Neural Network with Random Features for Transient Pressure Diffusion with Discontinuous and High-Contrast Coefficients
abstract: arXiv:2609.22349v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Transient pressure diffusion in heterogeneous porous media becomes difficult to resolve efficiently when permeability is discontinuous and spans several orders of magnitude. We develop a domain-decomposed random-feature evolutional deep neural network (DD RF-EDNN) that separates spatial approximation from temporal evolution. Permeability-informed random features are compressed into an orthonormal pressure space, and a conservative finite-volume operator is projected onto this space so that only the reduced coordinates are advanced in time. This formulation retains the dissipative structure of the discrete flow problem without repeated neural-network optimization. The analysis quantifies dictionary and singular-value truncation errors, proves contractivity under an energy-consistent dissipativity correction, and derives a conditional grid-level estimate for homogeneous dynamics and time-independent data admitting a steady lifting. translated_title: 用于具有不连续和高对比度系数的瞬态压力扩散的域分解随机特征演化深度神经网络
translated_abstract: 当渗透率不连续且跨越多个数量级时，非均质多孔介质中的瞬态压力扩散变得难以高效求解。我们开发了一种域分解随机特征演化深度神经网络（DD RF-EDNN），将空间近似与时间演化分离。基于渗透率信息的随机特征被压缩成一个正交压力空间，并将保守的有限体积算子投影到该空间上，使得只有降维后的坐标随时间推进。这种表述在无需重复神经网络优化的情况下保留了离散流动问题的耗散结构。分析量化了字典和奇异值截断误差，证明了在能量一致的耗散性修正下的收缩性，并对允许稳态提升的均匀动力学和时间无关数据推导了条件网格级估计。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种域分解随机特征演化深度神经网络（DD RF-EDNN），通过将基于渗透率信息的随机特征压缩到正交压力空间并投影保守有限体积算子，实现了空间近似与时间演化的分离，从而在无需重复神经网络优化的情况下高效求解渗透率不连续且高对比度的非均质多孔介质瞬态压力扩散问题，并保留了离散流动问题的耗散结构。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a domain-decomposed random-feature evolutional deep neural network (DD RF-EDNN) that separates spatial approximation from temporal evolution by compressing permeability-informed random features into an orthonormal pressure space and projecting a conservative finite-volume operator onto it, enabling efficient solution of transient pressure diffusion in heterogeneous porous media with discontinuous, high-contrast coefficients while retaining the dissipative structure of the discrete flow problem without repeated neural-network optimization.
